A death certificate — the primary target — would provide date, place, cause of death, and often parentage and birthplace, making this question the gatekeeper for both halves of the objective.

questions.question: Who were the parents of William Hubert Ferber (b. approximately December 1869, Ohio; husband of Emma Becker, Cincinnati, Hamilton County, Ohio)?
questions.rationale: The objective asks for ancestral origins of William H. Ferber. No parents are identified in the tree. The 1900 census shows him born December 1869 in Ohio with both parents also born in Ohio, suggesting a multi-generation Ohio family possibly of German descent given the surname. Q1 (death record) is the gatekeeper because William's death certificate will likely name his parents and their birthplaces; if it does, this question may resolve simultaneously. If the death cert lacks parentage, census records, vital records, and city directories from the 1860s–1880s will be needed.

items.rationale: Ohio's mandatory statewide death registration began 1 January 1908. FamilySearch collection 'Ohio, Deaths, 1908-1953' (3.5M indexed records + 3.9M images) is the primary indexed source for William's death certificate. A death certificate would give date, place, and cause of death, and typically names the informant plus the deceased's parents and their birthplaces — directly answering both the death and ancestry questions. William was last confirmed alive in Cincinnati city directories in 1910, making this the highest-probability first search.

FamilySearch 'Ohio, Death Index, 1908-1932, 1938-1944, and 1958-2007' (7.6M records, index-only) covers a broader date window than the image collection above and may surface death years not yet imaged. If the primary search (pli_001) yields no result, this index — covering gaps in 1933-1937 and 1945-1957 — may locate William's death year to direct targeted image retrieval from the county or state archives.

FamilySearch 'Ohio, County Death Records, 1840-2001' (2.1M records, 997K images) includes Hamilton County death registrations that may predate 1908 state-level registration and provides county-level granularity. If William died before 1908 or if the state-level index missed him (common for Ferber/variant spellings), the county register is the fallback. Also useful to verify the original image once a state death index entry is found.

Ancestry hosts Ohio death records from a different index than FamilySearch (collection 'Ohio Deaths, 1908-1953' and 'Ohio, Death Index' on Ancestry), and their OCR of the same microfilm often resolves name variants differently. If FS searches for 'Ferber' miss William due to indexing variations (Ferber/Feber/Ferbar), Ancestry's independent index provides a check — particularly important given that the surname 'Ferber' is uncommon enough to have few false positives but easy to mis-index.

items.jurisdiction: Cincinnati, Hamilton County, Ohio, United States
items.rationale: Charles Hubert Ferber (William's son) is buried at Spring Grove Cemetery, Cincinnati — one of the largest and most historically significant cemeteries in the US. William's wife Emma Becker is also noted with burial at Spring Grove (10 Dec 1948 in the tree). The family burial pattern makes it highly probable William is also interred there. Spring Grove Cemetery maintains online burial records at springgrove.org; FindAGrave and BillionGraves also index it. A burial record will give the interment date (within days of death) and often the deceased's age, providing a cross-check on the death certificate.

FamilySearch 'Ohio, Probate Records, 1789-1996' (mostly browse-only images, 7M images for Ohio) includes Hamilton County Probate Court wills, administrations, and estate files. If William left a will or died intestate with assets, there would be a Hamilton County probate filing. A will naming heirs establishes the death year and often names his wife Emma, children, and potentially siblings or parents. The probate file may also contain an inventory listing real property that corroborates his Cincinnati residence. Note: Hamilton County probate is largely browse-only — volume_search will be needed to identify relevant reels.

This is a FAN-directed item since the obituary would also name siblings, in-laws, and other relatives.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
# The Death of William H. Ferber, Cincinnati, Ohio, 1903

## Research Question

When and where did William Hubert Ferber (born approximately December 1869, Ohio; married Emma Becker, 10 September 1890, Hamilton County, Ohio; father of Charles Hubert Ferber, born 22 June 1891, Cincinnati) die, and what were the circumstances of his death?

## Evidence

### Ohio County Death Record (Primary Source)

A county death register entry for "Wm. Ferber" in Hamilton County, Ohio, accessed via FamilySearch "Ohio, County Death Records, 1840–2001" (collection 2128172), ark:/61903/1:1:F66M-8JZ, records:

- Deceased: Wm. Ferber, Male, White, Married  
- Death date: 11 March 1903  
- Death place: Cincinnati, Hamilton County, Ohio  
- Birth year/place: 1870, Cincinnati, Hamilton County, Ohio  
- Father: Gerhard Ferber; Mother: Eva Ferber

**Source classification:** original record (county death register, not a derivative). **Death date and place:** primary information — recorded contemporaneously by an official registrar or attending physician at the time of the event (source = original, information = primary, evidence = direct). **Birth year, parentage, marital status, race:** secondary information — reported by an unidentified personal informant (a family member) relaying biographical details they did not witness; classified original/secondary/indirect per standard death-certificate doctrine.

### Identity Correlation

The record persona "Wm. Ferber" was evaluated against the research subject G7JB-YH6 (William H. Ferber) using a FamilySearch same_person comparison (score: 0.737, strong tier). Side-by-side comparison:

| Attribute | Death Record | Subject |  
|-----------|--------------|---------|  
| Surname | Ferber | Ferber |  
| Given name | Wm. (standard abbr.) | William H. |  
| Birth year | 1870 | December 1869 |  
| Birth place | Cincinnati, Hamilton, Ohio | Ohio |  
| Marital status | Married | Married (Emma Becker, 1890) |  
| Death/last residence | Cincinnati, Hamilton, Ohio | Cincinnati (confirmed 1870–1900) |

The one-year difference in birth year is not a conflict: a December 1869 birth produces age 33 in March 1903, consistent with the record, and a registrar computing only the year would write 1870. All core identifiers agree. No disqualifying mismatch was found.

Circumstantially, Cincinnati city directory entries (FamilySearch "United States City and Business Directories," multiple years 1903–1910) attached to Emma Becker Ferber's person record (G7JB-2T6) place Emma in Cincinnati from 1903 onward under her own name — consistent with William having predeceased her. These entries are circumstantial; they do not supply an independent dated death record.

### Search Scope

Ohio's mandatory statewide death registration did not begin until 1 January 1908; a death on 11 March 1903 would not appear in the state-level collections (FamilySearch collections 1307272 and 1949341), explaining the absence found there. The county-level collection (pre-dating statehood registration) was the productive source.

The underlying original register image (ark:/61903/3:1:S3HT-66TS-SCS) could not be retrieved: the file is 1.1 MB, exceeding the MCP transport limit. The indexed transcription obtained via record_read captures the key columns. The cause of death was not returned in the indexed content; it may be absent from this register page, illegible, or not indexed — this remains an open gap in the circumstances.

Two independent-verification sources — a Spring Grove Cemetery burial record (FindAGrave, pli_005) and a Cincinnati newspaper obituary circa 11 March 1903 (Newspapers.com, pli_007) — were identified but could not be captured in this autonomous research run. URLs were generated and logged (log_006, log_007) for retrieval in an interactive session. Spring Grove Cemetery is the probable burial location given confirmed family interments there (Emma Becker Ferber, 10 December 1948; Charles Hubert Ferber, burial noted in tree). A consistent obituary and burial record would, when captured, advance this conclusion to proved.

## Conclusion

The preponderance of available evidence strongly indicates that **William Hubert Ferber died on 11 March 1903 in Cincinnati, Hamilton County, Ohio**. The conclusion rests on an original record carrying primary information on the death date and place — the strongest source class available for a death event. Identity is supported by a FamilySearch same_person score of 0.737 with no conflicting identifiers. No evidence suggests a different date, place, or individual.

The tier is **probable**, not proved: GPS proof requires at least two independent original sources with primary information, and only one was captured in this run. The cause of death remains unknown (original image inaccessible; cause not present in the indexed content). The deferred FindAGrave and Newspapers.com searches, which are accessible interactively, represent the natural path to advancing this conclusion to proved.
